title: A1: runner contract and single trust resolution
description:
# Sprint A1 — Runner contract and single trust resolution

## Objective

Establish the orchestration boundary every later sprint consumes: resolve one
trusted harness agent, invoke it with one typed fenced payload, validate its
single fenced response, and write a credential-safe attestation.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns registry resolution, runtime descriptors, invocation-envelope
validation, result-envelope validation, and attestation. It does not parse phase
plans, execute tracker commands, change Jev networking, or rewrite agent bodies.

## Dependency relations

- `must_follow` Sprint A0 because the runner may attest only anchors accepted by
  the calibrated bootstrap rubric.
- Sprint A2 is `must_follow` because its plan-source descriptor becomes an
  operation field in this runner contract.

## Public contract

```json
{
  "runtime": {
    "agent": "anchor-plan-review",
    "harness": "codex",
    "path": ".codex/agents/anchor-plan-review.md",
    "version": "0.5.0",
    "model": "luna",
    "sha256": "<64 lowercase hex characters>"
  },
  "operation": "plan_review",
  "correlation_id": "phase-a:A1"
}
```

The runtime path is registry-relative and confined to the selected plugin root.
The descriptor is immutable after resolution and contains no credential or
executable command string.

## Authoritative deliverables

- A deterministic resolver for Claude and Codex registries that validates
  plugin confinement, regular-file status, frontmatter identity/version,
  registry version, allowed role model, and SHA-256.
- A versioned JSON schema for the common runtime and operation envelope.
- Harness instructions that invoke the registered agent through Agent with
  exactly one fenced JSON params object.
- A response parser that accepts exactly one fenced JSON result and validates
  success and error envelopes before any follow-on action.
- A redacted attestation schema and atomic writer containing registry identity,
  version, model, file digest, source digest when supplied, correlation ID,
  timing, and outcome.
- Focused error codes for untrusted path, identity/version/model mismatch,
  changed hash, malformed params/result, timeout, and atomic-write failure.

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- Resolution and attestation occur once per agent invocation; no gate or tuner
  agent searches installation paths or repeats frontmatter trust validation.
- A supplied plugin root or registry entry that fails validation never falls
  back to another location.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, duplicated, or unfenced params/results fail
  closed before another operation begins.
- Claude and Codex invocation instructions use Agent and contain no active Task
  tool instruction.
- Resolver output, error text, and attestations contain neither credentials nor
  interpolated shell command strings.

## Authoritative validation

- Unit fixtures: valid Claude/Codex registry; traversal; symlink escape;
  non-regular file; wrong name/version/model; modified file hash; duplicate JSON
  fences; malformed response; timeout; failed atomic replace.
- Static assertion: gate and tuner definitions contain no installation search
  or independent registry/frontmatter validation after Sprint A5 lands.
- Secret canaries through successful, error, and timeout attestation paths.
- Existing `scripts/check_version_sync.py` and offline unit tests remain green.

## Traceability

- Phase requirements: PA-REQ-001–004, PA-REQ-013, PA-REQ-018.
- Locked anchors: ANC-001–002, ANC-012.
- Tracker: `pa-sza.1`.

## Risks and mitigations

- Harnesses expose different launch mechanisms: keep the shared descriptor
  identical and isolate only the thin Agent invocation wording.
- Attestation may leak inputs: record digests and typed metadata, not raw params
  or environment values.

## Non-closure

- Markdown phase/sprint discovery.
- `bd`/`br` execution.
- Agent-body simplification.
- General-purpose plugin execution outside plan-anchor.

## Handoff to A2

A2 consumes the envelope schema and adds a validated plan-source descriptor;
it does not reopen runtime trust rules.

title: A2: Markdown and tracker plan sources
description:
# Sprint A2 — Markdown and tracker plan sources

## Objective

Let `/plan-anchoring` review either a phase index plus linked Markdown sprint
documents or a copy of the same plan under a `bd`/`br` epic, using one normalized
item contract and explicit source parity checks.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns Markdown and tracker plan-source discovery, sprint ordering,
repository path confinement, structural checks, source revisions, normalized
digests, parity comparison, and item composition. It does not mutate tracker
state, tune questions, or change verdict semantics.

## Dependency relations

- `must_follow` Sprint A1 because the plan-source descriptor is validated as an
  operation-specific extension of the runner payload.
- Sprint A3 is `must_follow` because tracker records attach workflow metadata to
  the source descriptors established here.

## Invocation and source contract

Supported user-facing targets:

```text
/plan-anchoring docs/plans/phase-a/plan-phase-a.md
/plan-anchoring docs/plans/phase-a/
/plan-anchoring --tracker br --epic pa-sza
```

The directory form must resolve exactly one phase index. The phase index must
contain one sprint table whose plan links identify ordered repository-local
Markdown files. The tracker form must resolve one epic and its planning
children; each child description is an exact copy of one complete sprint
Markdown file. The adapter derives the sprint identifier from that document,
rejects missing or duplicate identifiers, and orders by the phase's sprint
identifier rather than tracker issue ID, creation time, or API return order.
Tracker title, acceptance, design, and notes remain workflow metadata. Both
forms produce the copied sprint Markdown plus source metadata as the normalized
item. Each Markdown sprint file must contain one
authoritative section each for deliverables, acceptance criteria, and validation,
plus explicit scope and non-closure. Paths to delete are required only when
deletion is in scope.

## Authoritative deliverables

- Plan-source adapters for a phase-index file/directory and a selected tracker
  epic, returning ordered sprint descriptors with source kind, phase/sprint ID,
  source reference/revision, normalized SHA-256, and dependency relation.
- Deterministic parsing of the phase sprint table without executing Markdown,
  HTML, links, code blocks, or repository content.
- Repository confinement and rejection of absolute, escaping, duplicate,
  missing, non-regular, or symlink-escaped sprint paths.
- Structural checks for exactly one authoritative deliverables, acceptance, and
  validation section in every sprint and for unique phase/sprint identifiers.
- Planning-item composition from the complete sprint file or tracker copy with
  a shared normalization function and no source-specific semantic rewriting.
- Canonical outbound-body construction that keeps source locators, tracker IDs,
  run IDs, and revisions outside the Jev request so equivalent Markdown and
  tracker items produce byte-identical JSON bodies.
- A copy/parity command that writes or verifies each complete sprint document in
  the tracker description, records the source path/digest, and refuses
  destructive overwrite when the target changed independently.
- Run metadata binding every verdict to the phase path, sprint path, Git commit
  when available, and SHA-256 reviewed.
- A `shape` path for sprint files that reports section sizes and detects plans
  too large for reliable review without silently trimming prose.

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- File, directory, and `pa-sza` tracker invocations discover the same ordered
  sprint set for this Phase A plan.
- A fresh tracker copy has the same normalized item digest as its Markdown
  source; independent drift fails parity before Jev is called.
- Every Jev request contains one normalized sprint item and one anchor, never
  the phase index/epic, intent, or another sprint.
- Direct, Markdown-agent, and tracker-agent construction of an equivalent item
  yields byte-identical canonical Jev JSON; equality is checked on the body that
  reaches the transport boundary, not on a lossy projection after execution.
- Invalid or ambiguous phase structures return typed errors before delegation.
- A sprint exceeding the reliable limit produces `PLAN.TOO_LARGE` plus shape
  evidence; no implementation truncates prose or raises the cap to pass.

## Authoritative validation

- Parser fixtures: valid phase file/directory and tracker epic; missing or duplicate index;
  malformed sprint table; duplicate ID/path; broken link; absolute/traversing
  path; symlink escape; missing authoritative section; duplicate checklist.
- Golden composition tests proving equivalent Markdown and tracker copies
  normalize identically, including headings, prose, and fenced examples.
- Differential request fixtures that materialize one item through Markdown,
  `bd`, and `br`, compare the exact serialized Jev body, and fail on source
  locator or tracker metadata leakage.
- Digest tests proving stable output, changed-content detection, and drift refusal.
- Dogfood discovery over `docs/plans/phase-a/plan-phase-a.md` returning A0–A7
  in table order.

## Traceability

- Phase requirements: PA-REQ-005–007.
- Anchors: ANC-015–016.
- Tracker: `pa-sza.2`.

## Risks and mitigations

- Markdown parsing grows into a general parser: support the explicit phase
  table and authoritative headings only; fail on ambiguity.
- Detailed contracts make a sprint too large: harden or split on a real
  production-ready boundary rather than hiding content from Jev.

## Non-closure

- Arbitrary Markdown plans without a phase index and sprint documents.
- Automatic rewriting or splitting of sprint documents.
- General tracker mutation beyond safe copy creation/parity verification.
- Development-gate evidence composition.

## Handoff to A3

A3 associates optional tracker identities, dependencies, question records, and
review comments with these immutable source descriptors while leaving their
Markdown content authoritative.

title: A3: tracker-neutral anchor and question store
description:
# Sprint A3 — Tracker-neutral anchor and question store

## Objective

Support a quickly initialized Go/Dolt `bd` or Rust/SQLite `br` store for anchors
and their plan/dev question records. Plan issues are optional and exist only when
the tracker-copy source from A2 is requested.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns initialization guidance, tracker selection, the five normalized
operations used by the anchor/question workflow, JSON normalization, and typed
tracker failures. It does not require plan work to be represented as issues.

## Dependency relations

- `must_follow` Sprint A2 so tracker objects reference established source
  descriptors rather than becoming a competing plan source.
- Sprint A4 is `must_follow` because its CLI/configuration cleanup exposes the
  explicit tracker-selection behavior implemented here.

## Normalized operation contract

| Operation | `bd` implementation | `br` implementation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show(id)` | `bd show ID --json` | `br show ID --json` | one issue object |
| `children(id)` | `bd children ID --json` | `br dep list ID --direction up --type parent-child --format json`, then `br show` | ordered issue array |
| `create(fields)` | fixed `bd create` argv | fixed `br create` argv | created issue identity |
| `update(id, fields)` | fixed `bd update` argv | fixed `br update` argv | updated issue identity/status |
| `comment(id, file)` | `bd comment ID --file FILE` | `br comments add ID --file FILE` | comment receipt |

## Authoritative deliverables

- A tracker descriptor and adapter exposing only `show`, `children`, `create`,
  `update`, and `comment` with typed fields and normalized JSON results.
- Explicit selection rules: a requested tracker wins after capability checks;
  otherwise exactly one valid repository workspace must be discovered.
- Canonical binary/workspace resolution once at the orchestration boundary and
  typed ambiguity, missing, unsupported-version, not-found, conflict, and
  malformed-output errors.
- Fixed subprocess argv construction with no shell and no command text accepted
  from agent params.
- `bd` and `br` fixture suites plus installed-binary integration tests guarded
  by binary availability.
- Disposable import/materialization helpers for differential tests that copy an
  authoritative Markdown sprint into `bd` and `br` without semantic rewriting
  or touching an existing project's production tracker database.
- Fast, documented initialization for a repository that needs only anchor and
  question records, without unrelated agent/hook installation side effects.
- Optional tracker plan-copy records carrying the source path and digest defined
  by A2; they are not created for ordinary Markdown-only review.

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- The same normalized contract tests pass for current supported `bd` and `br`
  fixture outputs.
- The registered plan-review agent can read question records through either
  adapter regardless of whether plan input is Markdown or a tracker copy.
- If both or neither valid tracker workspaces are available without an explicit
  selection, the adapter returns a typed error instead of guessing.
- Params containing shell command strings or unsupported operation names are
  rejected before process creation.
- A new repository can initialize a `br` anchor/question store, create one anchor
  tree, and validate it without first creating a phase epic or sprint issues.

## Authoritative validation

- Contract fixtures for array/object/envelope output, empty children, missing
  issue, version mismatch, ambiguity, malformed JSON, and nonzero exit.
- Command-injection tests over IDs, paths, comments, and unknown fields proving
  argv remains data and no shell is invoked.
- Installed-binary smoke tests for `show`, `children`, and a disposable create /
  update / comment lifecycle when the corresponding tracker is available.
- Regression proving the current `br` Phase A workspace no longer fails through
  a hard-coded `bd show` path.
- Known-plan regression that copies selected sc-lint sprint documents into
  disposable `bd` and `br` stores and proves both normalize to the same item
  bytes and ordering as Markdown.

## Traceability

- Phase requirements: PA-REQ-008–010.
- Locked anchors: ANC-013, ANC-016–018.
- Tracker: `pa-sza.3`.

## Risks and mitigations

- Similar command names conceal semantic differences: normalize explicit
  operations and test real emitted shapes; never interpolate command templates.
- Auto-selection chooses a stray installation: require a valid repository-local
  workspace and fail on ambiguity.

## Non-closure

- Database migration or shared on-disk format.
- General tracker operations unrelated to plan-anchor.
- Markdown parsing or mandatory plan-content projection into issue bodies.

## Handoff to A4

A4 exposes tracker choice through explicit arguments/defaults and removes the
remaining environment configuration without changing adapter semantics.

# Sprint A4 — Configuration and explicit offline behavior

## Objective

Make installation portable and network behavior evident from the command:
`TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is the only application environment input, live execution
needs no second opt-in, and offline paths provably never create transport.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns CLI configuration, environment reads, transport construction,
and offline-network tests. It does not change Jev question wording, verdict
semantics, retry policy, or plan/tracker discovery.

## Dependency relations

- `must_follow` Sprint A3 so source and tracker choices have stable explicit
  argument contracts before legacy environment paths are removed.
- Sprint A5 is `must_follow` because agent params use the final CLI behavior.

## Authoritative deliverables

- Remove reads of `PLAN_ANCHOR_ALLOW_REMOTE_JUDGE`, `PLAN_ANCHOR_JEV_URL`,
  `PLAN_ANCHOR_JEV_MODEL`, `PLAN_ANCHOR_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD`,
  `PLAN_ANCHOR_MAX_ITEM_CHARS`, `PLAN_ANCHOR_MAX_CODE_LINES`,
  `PLAN_ANCHOR_CONFIRM_NEAR`, and `USER` as an author default.
- Remove `--allow-remote`; a live command plus a valid `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` is
  sufficient authorization, while `--dry-run` is the explicit no-send mode.
- Retain or add explicit endpoint, model, threshold, size, confirmation, author,
  source, and tracker flags with checked-in defaults and stable help text.
- Centralize API-key validation at live transport construction and preserve
  recursive redaction of the raw key and bearer forms.
- Separate command preparation from transport creation so dry-run and
  fixture-answer execution require no key and instantiate no client.
- Migrate tests and examples away from ordinary configuration environment vars.

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- A static test finds exactly one plan-anchor-owned environment read:
  `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`.
- Live execution without the key fails with `AUTH.CREDENTIALS` before any
  transport call; live execution with the key needs no other opt-in.
- `--dry-run` and fixture-answer execution pass without a key and record zero
  transport constructions and calls.
- Help, errors, README, SKILL.md, agents, examples, and Jev references contain no
  active instruction for a removed variable or `--allow-remote`.
- Credential and bearer-token canaries are absent from stdout, stderr, nested
  exceptions, run files, reports, and attestations.

## Authoritative validation

- Transport-spy tests for live missing-key, live successful, dry-run,
  fixture-answer, retry, error, and report paths.

description:
# Sprint A5 — Harness-specific agent simplification

## Objective

Reduce each Claude and Codex agent to one gate or tuning responsibility after
runtime trust, Markdown source, tracker, and configuration decisions move to
their owning boundaries.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns the six harness-specific agent definitions and their registry
contracts. It preserves separate files and model roles and does not merge agents
or introduce sc-lint reviewers.

## Dependency relations

- `must_follow` Sprint A4 because agents consume the complete runtime, source,
  tracker, and configuration descriptors established in A1–A4.
- Sprint A6 is `must_follow` because it mechanizes the final agent contracts.

## Agent matrix

| Role | Claude model | Codex model | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anchor-plan-review` | Sonnet | Luna | Judge one authoritative sprint Markdown document against selected anchors. |
| `anchor-sprint-review` | Sonnet | Luna | Judge one delivered sprint evidence package and return deterministic checks. |
| `anchor-tuning` | Opus | Sol | Dedicated planner subagent: freeze the oracle, call Jev directly and in parallel over a candidate-question pool, down-select the production set with judgment, and independently triage disputed review failures. |

## Authoritative deliverables

- Update all six definitions to accept exactly one fenced params object using
  immutable runtime, plan-source/evidence, tracker, and operation descriptors.
- Replace `script` path hints, installation searches, and repeated registry /
  frontmatter checks with the pre-resolved runtime descriptor.
- Replace direct `bd`/`br` commands with normalized adapter operations and read
  planning item text from the bound sprint file, not a tracker description.
- Retain repository confinement for anchor, sprint, run, question, override, and
  evidence paths; keep one-operation responsibility and typed errors.
- Keep the tuner isolated from planner objectives and active plan verdicts; it
  freezes its oracle before the first Jev answer and returns auditable evidence.
  Preserve A0's explicit `testability` operation alongside the plan and
  development operations without sharing their verdict objectives.
- Replace the existing leaf `anchor-question-tune` profile and registry key with
  `anchor-tuning.md`. Register it as an Opus/Sol subagent of the planner in each
  harness. The tuner calls Jev directly; it does not need Agent/subagent
  capability and does not dispatch nested review workers.
- Define launch semantics for a stable named subagent instance
  `<team>-anchor-tuning`: start after the first draft and approved INTENT/ANC
  authority packet, run concurrently with continued planner work, expose status
  and evidence under that identity, and gate Sonnet/Luna review on its sealed
  question-set digests.
- Define distinct `tune` and `triage` schemas. `tune` excludes active plan text
  as normative authority and excludes any desired plan verdict. Its authority
  packet contains only approved intent and ANC records. It freezes the oracle
  before direct parallel Jev calls, generates multiple candidate questions per
  final role, and reserves candidate generation, ranking judgment, and
  down-selection for the tuner. An optional read-only plan descriptor is explicitly
  non-normative diagnostic corpus and may only be materialized as temporary
  mutations. `triage` accepts only a `sc-compose`-rendered evidence handoff and
  cannot accept a desired verdict or a proposed rewrite from the planner.
- Define the tuning tournament record: candidate ID and text, target role,
  frozen case IDs, raw role answers, derived verdicts, confidence, repeat
  stability, regressions, complexity, rank, rejection rationale, and selected
  production question. Every parallel call receives the same immutable
  candidate/corpus packet and returns raw evidence to the tuner.
- Keep the tuning pool out of normal review. Production `anchor-plan-review`
  requests contain only the down-selected role-complete question set; unselected
  candidates are audit evidence, never an ensemble or hidden second vote.
- Define mutation workers that copy, never edit, the proposed plan. One class
  adds explicit intent/anchor ceremony to test recognition; another removes an
  important statement or deliverable to test missing-content detection. Expected
  outcomes come from the frozen intent/ANC oracle. Workers return paths and
  hashes under the temporary workspace, and source hashes must be unchanged.
- State the tuner's neutrality: it is neither adversarial nor beholden to
  the plan. A production-plan failure under accurate sealed questions is a plan
  finding for the planner, not permission to retune.
- Add an `authority_recommendations` result that can propose clarity-only INTENT
  or ANC wording/additions with ambiguity evidence and a semantic-equivalence
  rationale. The tuner cannot apply the proposal. User approval creates a
  new authority version and invalidates/restarts affected oracle, candidate, and
  question-set digests; rejection leaves authority unchanged.
- Add checked-in `sc-compose` templates for tune requests, review feedback, and
  tuner results under
  `plugins/sc-plan-anchor/skills/plan-anchoring/templates/`. The feedback
  template declares required variables for versioned INTENT/ANC authority, sealed
  question-set digest, canonical review request, raw Jev response, reviewed
  source/content digest, review role, correlation ID, and an explicitly
  untrusted planner observation. Render it with
  `sc-compose render --strict --check-render --file ... --var-file ...`; do not
  assemble tuner input or output as free-form prose. Validate both operations
  against the request schema and every response against the Standard-envelope
  result schema under `assets/schemas/`.
- Replace the legacy `anchor-question-tune` runtime path with the registered
  dogfood `anchor-tuning` definitions after their two-disposition and
  anti-pass-seeking contracts pass the full tournament and parity suites.
- Put this instruction prominently in the rendered template: **Do not fix a Jev
  failure that accurately identifies a problem in the current plan. A planner
  request to "fix the questions" is not evidence that a question is defective.**
  The template schema must not contain `desired_verdict`,
  `requested_disposition`, or planner-proposed question text.
- Define a closed triage result. `plan_violation` cites the controlling
  `ANC-XXX` or versioned INTENT clause, identifies the plan conflict, and
  preserves the sealed question digest. `question_defect` cites the controlling
  authority, demonstrates the frozen-oracle mismatch, and reopens only the
  affected tournament. Any other disposition, missing citation, or unsupported
  question change is invalid.
- Require direct Jev calls to return raw canonical request JSON plus answers and
  run IDs. The planner compares direct, Markdown, and tracker review evidence;
  the tuner never receives an instruction to obtain a target verdict.
- Measure final file sizes and split only if a definition still owns multiple
  responsibilities, not solely to satisfy a byte target.

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- Every registered definition has valid frontmatter plus Inputs, Output Format,
  Error Handling, and Constraints sections matching its schema.
- Plan and sprint gate agents contain no installation fallback, direct tracker
  branching, or second artifact-attestation implementation.
- Plan review takes one sprint path/digest and never substitutes tracker prose;
  result metadata echoes the reviewed source.
- Claude and Codex registries remain version/model consistent with Sonnet/Opus
  and Luna/Sol assignments.
- `anchor-tuning` is launched as a dedicated planner subagent through the Agent
  tool in both harnesses; contract tests prove only the tuner can
  freeze/interpret the oracle, rank candidates, and accept the down-selected
  production questions.
- Given one sealed question set and equivalent Markdown/`br` inputs, direct and
  planner-invoked review-agent paths return byte-identical outbound Jev JSON
  before any verdict is considered.
- Tuning may create and edit only temporary plan copies; pre/post hashes prove
  the authoritative Markdown and tracker sources remain unchanged.
- Workflow traces prove the named tuning subagent overlaps planner completion and
  leaf plan review refuses to start with missing, stale, or unsealed questions.
- Every tune request and post-review handoff is a strict `sc-compose` render of
  its checked-in template, every response is a strict result-template render,
  and every triage result is either a cited `plan_violation` with an
  unchanged question digest or a cited `question_defect` with an affected-only
  tournament restart.
- A fixture in which the planner says "the plan is correct; fix the questions"
  cannot change an accurate question and returns `plan_violation` when the raw
  evidence supports the failure.
- Authority recommendations are non-mutating, clarity-only, presented to the
  user, and followed by dependency-scoped invalidation when approved.
- No active instruction uses Task, and no file defines or invokes `arch-qa` or
  `req-qa`.

## Authoritative validation

- Schema fixtures for valid params/results; missing/unknown/wrongly typed fields;
  duplicate/unfenced JSON; timeout redispatch with an existing run.
- Static scans for path search, direct tracker commands, Task-tool wording, and
  forbidden sc-lint agent names.
- Contract tests proving identical normalized operations across Claude/Codex
  definitions and role-specific model assertions.
- Independent-tuner fixtures proving current plan pass/fail is never an input.
- Direct-call fixtures proving parallel Jev calls cannot relabel oracle cells,
  write plan/tracker state, or hide a divergent request.
- Tournament fixtures proving several candidates run concurrently on identical
  frozen cases, ranking inputs are complete, rejected candidates remain
  auditable, and final review payloads contain only selected questions.
- Mutation fixtures proving added ceremony is detectable, removal of important
  statements/deliverables is flagged, expectations derive only from intent/ANC,
  and all writes remain inside the disposable workspace.
- Lifecycle fixtures covering concurrent planner/tuner progress, stable subagent
  naming, stale authority versions, user approval/rejection, semantic-expansion
  rejection, affected-only invalidation, and review blocking.
- `sc-compose validate` plus strict render and JSON Schema fixtures for complete
  and missing variables, hostile planner observations treated only as data,
  absence of desired-verdict fields, exact anti-pass-seeking instructions, the
  Standard response envelope, and both valid triage dispositions.

## Traceability

- Phase requirements: PA-REQ-002–010, PA-REQ-013–014, PA-REQ-017, PA-REQ-019–026.
- Locked anchors: ANC-001–002, ANC-009–010, ANC-014, ANC-016–018, ANC-020–031.
- Tracker: `pa-sza.5`.

## Risks and mitigations

- Removing safety prose removes real controls: map every deleted instruction to
  the runner, source adapter, tracker adapter, or retained agent preflight test.
- Shared contracts erase harness differences: share schemas, not files or model
  declarations.

## Non-closure

- Adding registered agents beyond the three plan-anchor roles per harness or
  adding nested agents beneath `anchor-tuning`.
- Changing plan/development question or verdict semantics; A0 owns the
  testability-rubric semantics that this sprint preserves.
- Refactoring unrelated marketplace or sc-lint agents.

## Handoff to A6

A6 converts these final contracts and every locked deterministic check into CI
assertions before documentation claims the behavior is shipped.

## Objective

Turn the architectural guideline, locked anchors, and A1–A5 public contracts
into executable checks that fail for the intended reason before release.

required production fixes uncovered by those tests but does not redesign the

- Enforce Agent-tool wording and reject active Task-tool instructions.
- Enforce the application environment allowlist and zero-network offline paths.
- Validate the Markdown phase/sprint source contract, structured invocation
  examples, response envelopes, and source-path/digest attestations.
- Add `bd` and `br` contract fixtures, installed-binary smoke hooks, ambiguity

- Add credential canaries across stdout, stderr, nested errors, reports,
  attestations, run files, and timeout/retry paths.
- Add bootstrap-rubric state-machine and recorded-answer tests for `testable`,

  disagreement resolution.
- Add duplicate-detection regression cases proving that shared provenance does
  not override distinct atomic statements while genuine statement overlap is
  still rejected.
- Add tuner-isolation tests proving `anchor-tuning tune` cannot receive an
  active plan as authority and `triage` cannot accept a desired verdict,
  requested disposition, or planner-proposed question text.
- Add tuning-tournament tests proving candidate questions are evaluated in
  parallel against identical frozen cases, rank components and rejection reasons
  are persisted, semantic judgment can reject a misleading high score, and only
  down-selected questions enter production review requests.
- Add neutral plan-mutation tests: ceremony is added and required content is
  removed only in temporary copies, expectations are traceable to intent/ANC,
  source hashes remain unchanged, and a real baseline-plan failure is reported
  for plan repair rather than used to retune questions.
- Add lifecycle tests proving `<team>-anchor-tuning` starts as a planner
  subagent after the first
  draft/approved authority packet, overlaps planner work, and seals current
  questions before Sonnet/Luna review can begin.
- Add authority-recommendation tests proving proposals are clarity-only and
  non-mutating, user approval is required, rejected proposals preserve versions,
  and approved changes invalidate/restart all and only affected tuning evidence.
- Add strict `sc-compose` and JSON Schema tests for tune requests, triage
  feedback, and tuner results covering declared variables, missing values,
  deterministic rendering, exactly one valid fenced JSON payload, the Standard
  response envelope, hostile planner text remaining inert data, the exact
  anti-pass-seeking instruction, and the absence of desired-verdict fields.

  the questions." When raw evidence supports the failure, the only valid result
  is a cited `plan_violation` with an unchanged question digest. When a frozen
  oracle proves a question defect, require a cited `question_defect` and
  affected-only tournament restart.
- Add differential request tests that compare direct and review-agent,
  Markdown, `bd`, and `br` canonical Jev JSON byte for byte and retain a typed
  root-cause record for every injected divergence.
- Preserve and run existing judge, coverage, diff, shape, redaction, and version

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- Every locked anchor's deterministic check maps to at least one named
  executable assertion, recorded in a traceability fixture.
- Negative fixtures fail on the expected typed error or validator rule rather
  than on unrelated setup.
- CI fails on a deliberately escaping Markdown path, tracker-body substitution,
  unfenced result, wrong model, forbidden env read, Task instruction, raw secret,
  or direct tracker branch in an agent.
- CI fails when the tuning profile declares nested Agent/subagent capability, a
  direct Jev call can change oracle/question state, source metadata enters a Jev
  body, or two equivalent source paths serialize different request JSON.
- CI fails when candidate evaluation changes the oracle/case set, omits a

- CI fails if review consumes default/stale questions while the named tuning
  subagent is incomplete, or if a recommendation changes meaning, bypasses the user,
  or reuses evidence from an earlier authority version.
- CI fails if planner-to-tuner review feedback bypasses the checked-in template,
  if the rendered prompt lacks the anti-pass-seeking instruction, if triage
  returns a third disposition or omits an INTENT/ANC citation, or if an accurate
  failure changes the sealed question digest.
- The complete offline suite and `scripts/check_version_sync.py` pass on a clean
  checkout with no API key or network.
- Test output and persisted fixtures contain no live credential or machine-only
  absolute path.

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s plugins/sc-plan-anchor/skills/plan-anchoring/tests -p 'test_*.py'`.

- `git diff --check` and secret-canary repository scan.
- Mutation fixtures for each prohibited condition listed in acceptance.
- `sc-compose validate --strict --lint --check-render` and strict sample renders
  of all three installed anchor-tuning templates, followed by JSON Schema
  validation of each extracted fenced payload.
- Recorded-answer differential fixtures from this Phase A plan and selected

  `br` stores.

- Locked anchors: ANC-001–002, ANC-005, ANC-009–018, ANC-020–031.

# Sprint A7 — Documentation, examples, and dogfood

## Objective

Make the public contract match shipped behavior and prove plan-anchor can review
this authoritative Phase A Markdown plan through its own independent tuner and
Jev-backed planning gate.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns public documentation, executable examples, migration notes,
question-tuning evidence, planning runs, triage diffs, and final coverage. It
does not weaken anchors, questions, size limits, or verdicts to obtain a pass.

## Dependency relations

- `must_follow` Sprint A6 because documentation and dogfood describe and execute
  the final mechanically enforced behavior.
- Final sprint; Phase A closes only after its acceptance criteria pass.

## Authoritative deliverables

- Update README, SKILL.md, installation/troubleshooting, Jev API, anchor and
  tracker layout, planning/development gate references, PRD, architecture
  diagrams, manifests, and changelog to the final contracts.
- Document phase-index, directory, and tracker-epic invocation; source parity;
  authoritative sprint sections; the anchor/question-only store; explicit
  flags; and offline behavior.
- Replace stale environment-variable, prose-invocation, tracker-body, and
  hard-coded `bd` examples with executable current examples for both harnesses
  and trackers.
- Render `anchors.md`, keep tracker question/evidence references linked, and
  include the Markdown-authority anchors added during dogfood.
- Document the pipelined lifecycle: first draft and approved INTENT/ANC launch a
  named `<team>-anchor-tuning` subagent, planner completion proceeds concurrently,
  and Sonnet/Luna leaf review waits for sealed current-version questions.
- Verify A0's frozen bootstrap corpus and acceptance evidence, then run the
  calibrated rubric against every locked anchor before plan-question tuning.
- Run `anchor-tuning tune` for every non-structural anchor/gate, record the

  selection rationales, acceptance table, worker run IDs, and sealed production
  question-set digest in `question-tuning-evidence.md`; apply only the
  tuner's down-selection whose normative inputs are only approved intent
  and ANC records and whose objective is accurate detection, never plan passage.

  add explicit ceremony to positive copies and remove important statements or
  deliverables from negative copies. Record mutation hashes and expected
  outcomes, prove Markdown/`br` sources remain unchanged, and describe this as
  neutral calibration rather than adversarial review.

  `anchor-plan-review` over the Markdown and exact `br` copies with the sealed

  removed required content, and pre/post hashes prove no authoritative plan or
  tracker source was changed by the tuner.
- Both harnesses expose a dedicated Opus/Sol `anchor-tuning.md` planner

  planner refuses to invoke Sonnet/Luna leaves until all applicable
  question-set digests match the current INTENT/ANC versions.

  byte-identical outbound request JSON across direct and leaf-agent
  paths; recorded-answer parity runs have identical verdicts, and phase coverage
  has no uncovered anchor.
- The selected sc-lint corpus produces equivalent ordered plan items, requests,
  and recorded-answer verdicts through Markdown, disposable `bd`, and disposable
  `br` sources; every live divergence is classified and retained.
- Every failing-to-passing edit that grew cites a locked ANC/REQ/ADR that
  predates the failed run; otherwise the fix cuts or replaces text.
- Every planner-to-tuner review handoff is a strict render of the checked-in
  `sc-compose` template. Every triage result cites INTENT/ANC and is exactly
  `plan_violation` with an unchanged digest or `question_defect` with an
  affected-only tournament restart.
- The full offline suite, live dogfood evidence, and `gh stack view --json`
  report a clean, mergeable Phase A implementation stack.

- Execute all README and reference command examples in temporary repositories
  against recorded and installed supported tracker versions.
- Run `validate`, `lint`, `dedupe`, `render`, source discovery, independent
  `check-fixtures`, direct per-sprint Jev construction, `anchor-tuning tune`,
  strict template rendering, planner-invoked leaf review, disputed-failure
  triage, `diff`, and `coverage`.
- Run the A6 offline suite and version validator after the final documentation
  edits.
- Verify no secret appears in Git diff, logs, reports, run files, comments, or
  attestations.
- Verify the final PR stack with `gh stack view --json` and GitHub checks.

## Traceability

- Phase requirements: PA-REQ-001–026.
- Locked anchors: ANC-001–002, ANC-005, ANC-009–018, ANC-020–031.
- Tracker: `pa-sza.7`.

## Risks and mitigations

  strict `sc-compose` evidence packet; the tuner returns the closed binary

- Mutation tests are mistaken for adversarial plan editing: the authority packet

- Documentation repeats scope inconsistently: sprint plans remain authoritative;
  examples demonstrate contracts without restating deliverable checklists.
- Live requests expose secrets or excessive context: send only one anchor and

## Non-closure

- Adding unrelated marketplace work or sc-lint agents.
- Writing test copies into sc-lint's live `bd` or `br` database.
- Starting Phase B implementation.

## Phase handoff

Close Phase A only when every acceptance criterion in the phase index and this
sprint is satisfied. File explicit dependent work for any remaining finding;
do not carry it silently into implementation or Phase B.

# Sprint A0 — Bootstrap rubric calibration

## Objective

Make the testability rubric a trustworthy prerequisite for anchor capture by
calibrating its questions and confidence handling against a frozen,
plan-independent oracle before it judges this Phase A plan.

## Scope boundary

This sprint owns the versioned testability questions, their deterministic lint
seam, confirmation semantics, the calibration corpus, and the tuner's
`testability` operation. It does not tune plan/development questions, review the
active Phase A plan, or change plan/development verdict semantics.

## Dependency relations

- Root sprint; follows the Phase A base on `main`.
- Sprint A1 is `must_follow` because every later contract and dogfood run relies
  on anchors admitted by this calibrated bootstrap gate.

## Authoritative deliverables

- A frozen, versioned calibration corpus whose cases and expected answers are
  written before any Jev response and are unrelated to the active Phase A plan.
- Corpus coverage for valid directives, prohibitions, structural and global
  scope, one atomic anchor extracted from a multi-directive quote, genuinely
  bundled statements, unsupported elaboration, vague outcomes, explicit
  testable conditions, and API-key-output redaction.
- Testability questions that judge separately actionable constraints,
  observable artifacts or behavior, quote-supported obligations, identifiable
  scope, and self-contained conditions without requiring literal token matches.
- Deterministic requirement-form lint rather than a stochastic grammar vote.
- Duplicate detection that compares the testable statements, not only their
  provenance quotes, so two distinct atomic anchors may cite the same
  multi-directive user statement without being mislabeled as duplicates.
- Confirmation that runs each semantic cell twice and a third time on
  disagreement; low-confidence agreement is `inconclusive`, disagreement is
  `unstable`, and neither is misreported as evidence that wording is wrong.
- A `testability` operation in the independent Opus/Sol question-tuner contract
  that receives approved intent and the frozen corpus but no active-plan
  verdict, and returns corpus/rubric digests, rationales, attempts, disagreement
  data, and an acceptance table.
- Parallel candidate evaluation for the rubric questions: the tuning subagent tests
  more candidate wordings than the released rubric will use, ranks each against
  the same frozen corpus, and down-selects a role-complete final set using both
  measured evidence and independent semantic judgment.
- Neutral mutation cases derived only from intent/ANC authority: disposable
  plan-shaped text adds explicit ceremony for a required fact or removes a
  required statement/deliverable, proving the rubric recognizes both presence
  and absence without editing or taking sides on an authoritative plan.

## Authoritative acceptance criteria

- The frozen corpus and expected labels are hashed before the first Jev call;
  no case is added, removed, or relabeled after a response.
- Candidate questions are evaluated in parallel against identical frozen cases;
  the record preserves every candidate, score component, rejection rationale,
  and the tuning subagent's reason for the final down-selection.
- Hashes prove all mutation cases were temporary and no authoritative plan or
  tracker record changed during calibration.
- Every accepted rubric cell has two confident agreeing answers matching the
  oracle, with a third call used only to resolve disagreement.
- Confirmed `no` or `unclear` yields `needs_work`; low confidence yields
  `inconclusive`; conflicting confirmations yield `unstable`.
- An atomic anchor drawn from a multi-directive quote may pass when every
  obligation in the statement is supported by the quote; it need not exhaust
  unrelated directives in that quote.
- Two anchors with the same immutable quote are not duplicates when their
  normalized testable statements express distinct obligations; genuinely
  overlapping statements remain a failing duplicate pair.
- Explicit prohibitions and testable conditions may pass the self-contained
  criterion without being rewritten into misleading positive prose.
- The redaction case distinguishes compliant from violating output through an
  input/action/outcome test and does not depend on literal statement tokens.

## Authoritative validation

- Offline state-machine tests for two-call agreement, third-call tie breaking,
  `testable`, `needs_work`, `inconclusive`, and `unstable`.
- Recorded-answer corpus tests for every required case and each semantic cell.
- Live independent Sol/Opus calibration with persisted corpus digest, rubric
  digest, expected answers, rationales, all run IDs, and final acceptance table.
- Mutation cases for a bundled statement, unsupported policy, vague outcome,
  private shorthand, unrecorded approval dependency, two atomic anchors sharing
  one quote, and two genuinely duplicate statements with different quotes.

## Traceability

- Phase requirement: PA-REQ-018.
- Anchors: none; this is the bootstrap instrument that determines whether an
  anchor is fit to enter later gates.
- Tracker: `pa-sza.8`.

## Risks and mitigations

- Calibration overfits Phase A: exclude active-plan text and use unrelated
  corpus cases with frozen rationales.
- Repeated calls hide uncertainty: preserve every answer and disagreement;
  confirmation classifies instability rather than averaging it away.
- Rubric work drifts into plan verdict changes: keep plan/development question
  IDs, roles, thresholds, and `decide()` semantics out of this sprint.

## Non-closure

- Tuning any Phase A plan or development question.
- Lowering a threshold to turn an inconclusive answer into a pass.
- Changing plan/development verdict meanings or coverage policy.
- Reviewing Markdown or tracker plan sources.

## Handoff to A1

A1 consumes only anchors accepted by the calibrated bootstrap gate and records
the rubric/corpus versions in the invocation attestation; it does not reopen
testability semantics.
